bottleneck: Engineered genetic circuits that perform beautifully in the lab lose function inside the body: mutation, epigenetic silencing, immune pressure, and the noisy in vivo environment degrade performance over weeks to months. Evolutionary pressure actively selects against circuits that burden the host cell, so function decays precisely when therapy needs to persist. Living therapeutics that must sense, compute, and act inside patients cannot be recalled or reprogrammed once deployed, so circuit failure means therapy failure with no recovery option.
current_state: Researchers are building mutation-resistant circuit architectures, kill switches, and closed-loop regulation, but long-term in vivo stability is still demonstrated only in short animal studies. Human data does not exist.

sources.title: Architecting the Future of Health: From Code to Cure

title: Synthetic gene circuits degrade inside the body
why_it_blocks: Programmable cell therapies are the future of medicine, but a program that corrupts itself in vivo is not a medicine. Circuit instability blocks smart therapeutics from leaving the lab, no matter how elegant the design.
